clauses.reason: Sec. 3(b) provides that, notwithstanding the order, the President retains discretion, to the extent permitted by Subchapter III of Chapter 33 of title 5, to depart from the order in designating an acting Secretary. It is a standing reservation with no end date, and the only held amendment (EO 13261) replaces Sec. 3(a) only.

Sec. 4 of the held original provides that the order it identifies as Executive Order 11274 (dated March 30, 1996 as printed in the held text) is hereby revoked. It is a one-time self-executing command with no effective date other than the order's own date, so it was performed when the order was signed on 2001-12-18 (the order was published in the Federal Register on 2001-12-21); the order's own registered clause is the source of the end. Nothing in the held evidence shows an earlier performance or a later reinstatement. The revocation of the earlier order does not affect the standing succession provisions of this order, which are decided separately.

research_rationale:
EO 13243 (66 FR 66262) of December 18, 2001 provides an order of succession within the Department of Housing and Urban Development. The held original was read in full and confirmed to be the order (number, date and subject agree with the register row). Sec. 3(a) was replaced by EO 13261 Sec. 4(c) of March 19, 2002, which is recorded as a later event on both fragments of Sec. 3(a) with the before-and-after text; Sec. 4, a one-time revocation of an earlier succession order, was performed on signing; the remaining fourteen clauses are standing succession provisions. The three bounded searches found only EO 13261 as a later instrument, so the order is carried as operative through 2026-10-14.
